newsitem.title: USA: U.S. airlines cut summer and fall fares.
newsitem.headline: U.S. airlines cut summer and fall fares.

text.p: U.S. airlines said Tuesday they will cut certain summer and fall airfares up to 45 percent, following a fare sale started by United Airlines.
United, a unit of UAL Corp, said it cut fares up to 45 percent from 21-day advance purchase levels for travel in the U.S., Canada, and selected Pacific markets.
The sale begins immedidately and is available through July 11. Domestic travel must be completed between July 14 and November 19; international travel must be completed by December 12, United said.
The fares require roundtrip purchase at least 14 days in advance of travel and a Saturday night stay. Other restrictions apply.
Continental Airlines Inc, Northwest Airlines Corp, Trans World Airlines Inc each said they will match the fare discount in markets where they compete with United.
US Airways Group Inc said it expanded the sale to apply to all of its U.S. and Canadian routes, as well as a portion of its San Juan service.
Delta Air Lines Inc and AMR Corp's American Airlines did not immediately return calls seeking comment.
